claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.

experiment_recipes.goal: Replicate near-perfect editing on COUNTERFACT under standard eval
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Edit evaluation on COUNTERFACT/ZSRE with Reliability/Generalization/Locality
metrics: Score (harmonic mean of Efficacy, Generalization, Specificity)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On 200 randomly sampled base-model-recallable COUNTERFACT edits (95% CI half-width ≤ 3%), MEMIT must achieve Score ≥ 90 and Reliability ≥ 90. Otherwise, refute the 'near-perfect' premise and halt downstream 'realistic evaluation' tests tied to this premise.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Cheap replication of prior headline results to establish the premise that near-perfect editing exists under standard (less realistic) evaluation.

experiment_recipes.goal: Validate PC geometry at edited layers
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: At the primary MEMIT-edited layer(s), mean cosine similarity between residual-stream activations and their top-256-PC reconstruction ≥ 0.90, and mean cosine similarity between activations and their bottom-10%-PC-only reconstruction ≤ 0.20, on a held-out Wikipedia split. Otherwise, the low-variance subspace is not well separated and this apparatus is invalid.
constraints_not_enforced: No layer sweep beyond edited layers
experiment_recipes.rationale: Builds and validates a geometry apparatus so low- vs high-variance directions are well defined for downstream causal tests.

experiment_recipes.goal: Realistic reliability/capability evaluation for MEMIT on RippleEdits
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: After sequentially applying k=100 edits: support the claim if ANY of the following hold: Reliability < 70% (RippleEdits), or Perplexity on Wikipedia increases > 10% vs base, or Instance-wise accuracy drops > 2.0 points on both HellaSwag and LAMBADA vs base, or NKL > 0.10, or Locality drops > 5 points. Refute the claim if ALL of the following hold: Reliability ≥ 80, Perplexity increase ≤ 5%, Instance-wise accuracy drop ≤ 1.0 point on both HellaSwag and LAMBADA, NKL ≤ 0.05, and Locality drop ≤ 2 points.
constraints_not_enforced: No batch editing at k=1000 or 3000
depends_on: Replicate near-perfect editing on COUNTERFACT under standard eval
experiment_recipes.rationale: Enforces realistic, ripple-aware evaluation and checks for degradation of core LM abilities post-edit, which directly tests the claim.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test geometric amplification of edits along low-variance directions via causal interventions
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Across 100 edited COUNTERFACT cases, at the primary edited layer: equal-norm interventions along bottom-10% PCs produce ≥ 2.0× larger mean Change in target token probability than equal-norm interventions along top-10% PCs in the edited model, AND the bottom-10% PC AIE increases by ≥ 50% vs the pre-edit model. Otherwise, refute the 'geometric limitation' component of the claim.
constraints_not_enforced: No multi-layer aggregation beyond edited layer(s)
depends_on: Validate PC geometry at edited layers
experiment_recipes.rationale: Uses standard causal tracing and IE metrics to attribute disproportionate amplification to low-variance directions, directly testing the geometric mechanism.

experiment_recipes.goal: Non-parameter editing control (IKE) shows no capability damage
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On the same 100-edit RippleEdits sample (evaluated per query, no weight changes), IKE must achieve Reliability ≥ 60 while Perplexity change on Wikipedia ≤ 2% and Instance-wise accuracy drops on HellaSwag and LAMBADA each ≤ 0.5 points vs base. If this holds while Recipe 'Realistic reliability/capability evaluation for MEMIT on RippleEdits' indicates capability damage, attribute damage to parameter updates; if it fails, refute this attribution.
depends_on: Realistic reliability/capability evaluation for MEMIT on RippleEdits
experiment_recipes.rationale: Removes the claim’s mechanism (weight edits) to ensure observed damage is not an artifact of evaluation prompts or datasets.

experiment_recipes.goal: Ablation: compare constrained FT (L-infinity) vs unconstrained FT at matched efficacy
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: At matched Efficacy within ±5% of unconstrained Fine-Tuning (FT), FT+L must reduce NKL by ≥ 30% and cut any Instance-wise accuracy drops on HellaSwag and LAMBADA by ≥ 50% relative to FT after k=100 sequential edits. If even FT+L still causes > 2.0-point accuracy drops on either dataset or > 10% Perplexity increase, this additionally supports the 'cannot update without damaging' clause; otherwise refute it.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Matched-budget ablation within parameter editing to test whether constraining update geometry mitigates damage; persistence of damage supports the claim.
